Content:
Former BYU RB Jamaal Williams joined @espnthefan to discuss the rivalry and NFL Free Agency:

Q: When did you move here permanently? How long have you been in Utah, and how’s that transition been — especially coming from the offseason down in New Orleans?

Jamaal: Well, honestly, ever since I got to BYU, I’ve always lived here. Even during the offseasons, I stayed. I always knew I’d make Utah home. I’ve got family here — some who lived on campus when I was at BYU, and more family in South Jordan. So it was natural for me to stick around.

And man, I love it here. Utah’s where I learned about genuine family — real, unconditional love. People who care about you as a person, not just for what you’ve done or the accolades you have. I love that they treat me like a normal dude.

Plus, my daughter’s out here — she’s a true Utahn. She made me into one. I moved closer just so I could be near her. She’s got her dad around now, and that’s the best thing ever.

The other day I went to her middle school — they had a little “walk-a-thon” thing, kids just walking around the block. Tell me why I ran it three times! (laughs) First time was with her — told her, “I’m gonna beat you!” Second time, some little kids came up like, “Hey, you’re Jamaal Williams! Wanna race?” And I’m like, “Bet.” You know I can’t turn that down. Beat them too. Third time my daughter’s like, “Let’s go again.” And I’m like, “Alright, fine!” Beat her again.

Then I’m exhausted — and suddenly all these little kids are crowding me, pulling out shoes, papers, whatever, asking for autographs. I’m like, “Y’all too young to even know who I am!” But some of them really did. That’s when you know you’re getting old — when kids say, “I used to watch you when I was little!” (laughs)

But it’s the best, man. My daughter’s face when people come up to me is hilarious — she’s like, “Can y’all back up? That’s MY dad.” I love every second of it.

I’m always respectful, though. I’m grateful for anyone who wants a picture or autograph. But really, I just love being out here — being close to her, being part of the community.

Q: You know BYU fans love you, man. Cougar Nation still shows you a ton of love — especially when you pop up at games.

Jamaal: (laughs) Those are paid actors! I paid Ronald Weaver to say all that nice stuff.

Q: Nah, they love you, man. It’s been awesome seeing you at BYU games, supporting the boys. You’re close with Tyler, you’ve watched LJ run the ball — what’s that been like?

Jamaal: Man, I love watching those guys. When LJ breaks runs, I’m over there like, “Boy, you better take that to the house!” (laughs) I remember being the young guy, getting that same push from the older dudes.

When I was at BYU, Harvey Unga was that for me We’d be running drills, and Harvey was teaching us everything he knew. That’s what I try to do for the younger backs now. Just be that support system.

I tell them all the time, “Ask me anything.” I love coming back to campus, working out, staying ready. Free agency is what it is right now, but I’m blessed to have a place like BYU where I can train, stay in shape, and keep my mindset right.

Q: I love that, man. Blessings to you and the fam. I mean, your NFL career’s been incredible — especially that Detroit year under Coach Dan Campbell. Seventeen touchdowns, breaking Barry Sanders’ record… unreal.

Jamaal: I give all that credit to my O-line, Coach Campbell, Ben Johnson, and Deuce Staley. They believed in me and knew how to use my strengths. They put me in position to succeed. I’ll always be grateful for that.

Q: You’ve always had that violent, downhill running style — fearless, physical. That’s been you since high school in Fontana.

Jamaal: (laughs) Yeah man, that’s just me. Run through faces — that’s what I do.

Item 2. Prohibited Contact. Brown has cleared this line in 5/6 (83%) this season while averaging 7.33 REC (7.5 MED). This is no anomaly either, Amon-Ra has hit the over on receptions in 70% of his games since 2023 when the line is set at 6.5 or lower. ☠☠️ 

The matchup here is golden as TBs secondary has been a liability this season. They rank in the bottom pack for REC yard defense (23rd). The Bucs' defense, under Todd Bowles, relies on aggressive blitzing. This often leaves underneath routes exposed where St. Brown excels. Amon-Ra has feasted on the Buccaneers in the past, grabbing 23 REC for 243 yards and a TD over 2 career meetings.

The game script here also works well with this play. As home favorites (-5.5) in a dome this should ensure a pass friendly game script. In a back and fourth battle, pass volume will raise on both sides. If that happens, St. Browns 3rd down reliability will shine as he has converted 80%.

Best Bets for College Football & NFL this weekend      

COLLEGE
Duke -2.5 vs GT (Best)
Tennessee +8 @ Alabama
Georgia -7 vs Ole Miss

NFL
LAC -1.5 vs IND (Best)
TEN +7 vs NE
LV +13 @ KC

NFL Survivor Pick: Denver Broncos

Notes
- Been on rough College stretch recently. Need to get back to 2-1s/3-0s. Lot of games I like this week. I picked my 3 favorites. We'll see how it goes!

- I've labeled GT for weeks as overrated. Turns out the Clemson win was not that impressive. Duke at home will be fired up taking on a ranked undefeated conference opponent. Duke can score. If they can limit the turnover I like them at home to pull the upset.. 

- Alabama win but I dont see them covering the -8 vs Tennessee. I think this will be a high scoring game. While good, this is not the Nick Saban Alabama team. They are different and that defense is not the same. Tennessee has a legit team who can put up points. Give me TEN +8 but I do believe Alabama ends up winning. 

- I think Georgia has been getting undervalued and ive said all year Ole Miss (while good) is overvalued. I think  Georgia would win this on a neutral field. At home, give me the Bulldogs. - Like the Chargers at home -1.5 vs IND who I dont believe are as a good as their record says they are. Steichen is a fantastic coach who is doing a great job with what he has but im not betting on Daniel Jones. Sorry. Harbaugh will have the team ready and I like the LAC to win and cover. 

- Classic Pros vs Joes spot here. Public heavy on the Patriots. Pros coming in on the Titans. Teams who switch coaches tend to do well that first game. NE may win the game but I think its going to be a dogfight and closely contested. Give me TEN +7. 

- LV +13. I know its disgusting betting on the Raiders but they play the Chiefs tough. I think LV has a better coach & QB than previous years even though Geno has been inconsistent. Betting double-digit division underdogs in the NFL is a strong bet most of the time. I expect the Chiefs to win but it wont be as easy as people think. Give me LV +13. 

- Survivor: I badly wanted to take the Bears here but I have a bad feeling. Saints arent good but have been playing better lately and Bears have barely squeaked by the last 2 weeks winning both games by 1pt. I just have a feeling I could get bit here. Good luck this weekend. Win some money!

10/19 - Sunday
Colts @ Chargers
🏈NFL🏈

1u - K. Allen (LAC) 5+ REC (-135 DK)

Show some love if you want more early lines before they move!❤️

The chargers seem to have found their rhythm this season coming into this game 4-2 as slight favorites at home. Their offense has been notable with Herbert distributing the ball very effectively so far. When he has effective targets like 6 time Pro Bowler Keenan Allen, it makes things much easier. Throughout the first 6 weeks Allen is over this line in 5/6 (83%) while averaging 5.5 REC (5 MED). So far, he has been averaging 8.5 targets a game with a 65% REC rate (5.5 REC). Last game (vs. MIA) he missed with 4 REC but was under his catch rate for that game (57%) dropping 3 of his 7 targets.

The chargers are passing way above league average with a 62% pass rate, with Herberts pass attempt line is set to 34.5 for this game. Assuming Allen tracks with his target share (23.8%) and given matchup / game script, the time machine has him for ~9 targets / ~6 REC. 

Not to mention, "third-and-Keenan" is a very real thing as Allen was almost top in the NFL with 100 third- and fourth-down conversions via reception during 2020-2023 (with Herbert), second only to Tyreek Hill.

The matchup here is gold as INDs secondary ranks near bottom for REC yards defense to opposing WRs (29th). However, the real vulnerability is in volume. They've allowed multiple receivers to rack up catches going over their lines in nearly every outing. IND has given up 300+ pass yards to two different QBs already (Brisset (ARI) 320 yards & Stafford (LA) 375 yards) often struggling with underneath routes where Allen thrives.

Content:
Behind-the-Scenes Footage of Jordon Hudson and Bill Belichick Revealed

Journalist Pablo Torre has uncovered new behind-the-scenes footage highlighting the dynamic between NFL legend Bill Belichick and Jordon Hudson. The footage, from the set of Belichick’s now-discontinued show Coach at NFL Films Studios, also features former Patriots defensive coordinator Matt Patricia and several producers.

In the videos, Hudson, who manages the North Carolina coach’s off-field opportunities, is seen questioning aspects of the show’s topics and graphics, showing clear skepticism. At one point, both Hudson, 24, and Belichick, 73, express frustration with NFL Films employees.

"I don’t know how they have four full-time graphics people," Hudson remarked, to which Belichick responded, "They can’t do s–t." Hudson agreed.

The show Coach, intended as an in-depth football analysis platform featuring Belichick, Patricia, and Michael Lombardi, has been discontinued since Belichick returned to coaching. Lombardi now serves as UNC football’s general manager.

The couple previously made headlines in April when Hudson interrupted Belichick during a CBS Sunday Morning interview, raising questions about her influence on his career. Torre’s investigation suggested that Belichick’s family was concerned about Hudson’s involvement, although UNC denied claims that she was banned from athletic facilities.

Belichick and Hudson publicly acknowledged their relationship last summer after first meeting on a flight in 2021

Crazy news: Before trading up with the #Jets in the 2024 NFL Draft to land QB J.J. McCarthy, the #Vikings had offered the #Patriots “a haul” on draft night—trying to land QB Drake Maye. 

Albert Breer: “The opportunity was there for a team riddled with holes to build up capital by using the No. 3 pick as a trade chip,” Breer wrote of New England. 

“The #Vikings offered the #Patriots the 11th pick, the 23rd pick and their 2025 first-round pick (along with Day 3 pick swaps that favored Minnesota) to go up eight spots to No. 3 and get Maye.”

The #Patriots ultimately turned down the offer from Minnesota, and a proposal from the #Giants for a 2025 first-round pick to move from No. 6 to No. 3, having conviction that the North Carolina standout would be a success in the league. It’s worked out so far for New England this season, as Maye has the #Patriots tied with the #Bills for first place in the AFC East after six games.

Very interesting stuff here. 👀

🏈 المنافسة في السوق الأمريكي:

كانت المنافسة الرئيسية في الولايات المتحدة من دوري كرة القدم الأمريكية (NFL)، حيث:

مباراة سينسيناتي بنغلس ضد بالتيمور ريفنز على قناة ABC جذبت
👥 13,393,000 مشاهد
📊 تصنيف 3.21 في فئة 18–49

مباراة نيويورك جِتس ضد ميامي دولفنز على ESPN سجلت
👥 8,464,000 مشاهد
📊 تصنيف 2.51 في فئة 18–49

بذلك بلغ متوسط المشاهدة خلال الفترة المتداخلة مع بث Raw (من 8:15 إلى 10:21 مساءً) حوالي 21.4 مليون مشاهد — أي أن WWE واجهت منافسة ضخمة جدًا من كرة القدم الأمريكية في ذلك التوقيت.

---

📊 أداء Raw على نتفليكس:

جاء عرض Raw في المركز الثامن بين البرامج التلفزيونية الإنجليزية الأكثر مشاهدة على نتفليكس خلال الأسبوع ، وسيظل في المركز نفسه حتى بعد أي تعديلات حسابية.

أما بين جميع البرامج على المنصة (بما في ذلك غير الإنجليزية)، فقد احتل أقصى ما يمكن أن يحققه المركز 32 ، إذ جاء في المرتبة 22 ضمن البرامج فقط (دون الأفلام الإنجليزية)، بينما حقق الفيلم الإنجليزي رقم 10 في الأسبوع 2.1 مليون مشاهدة.

---

🇺🇸 مقارنة بالسنة الماضية:

مقارنةً بعروض Raw على قناة USA Network في الفترة نفسها من العام الماضي:

انخفضت المشاهدات الأسبوعية الإجمالية بنسبة 38.3٪

أما المشاهدة المباشرة وفي نفس اليوم (ما يعادل أرقام نيلسن) فانخفضت بنسبة 51.8٪

يُذكر أن الانخفاض الفعلي أكبر من ذلك لأن بيانات نتفليكس تحتسب إعادة المشاهدة ضمن الأرقام ، بينما نظام نيلسن لا يحتسب المشاهدات المكررة.

---

🌍 الترتيب العالمي حسب الدول:

من بين ثماني دول تمت متابعتها ، دخل Raw قائمة أفضل 10 برامج فقط في ثلاث دول — وهو رقم قياسي منخفض جديد.

🇺🇸 الولايات المتحدة: المركز السابع (هبوطًا من الرابع الأسبوع السابق)

🇨🇦 كندا: المركز السابع (نفس المركز السابق)

🇬🇧 المملكة المتحدة: المركز التاسع (تحسنًا من العاشر الأسبوع السابق)

بينما خرج من المراكز العشرة الأولى في:

🇲🇽 المكسيك (كان التاسع الأسبوع الماضي)

🇮🇳 الهند (كان الثامن الأسبوع الماضي)

🇦🇺 أستراليا، 🇳🇿 نيوزيلندا، 🇸🇦 السعودية (لم يدخل القائمة في عرضي 9/22 و9/29)

---

📅 عرض 6 أكتوبر (10/6):

في المشاهدة المباشرة ونفس اليوم ، جاء ترتيب Raw على النحو التالي:

🇺🇸 الولايات المتحدة: المركز الثاني (هبوطًا من الأول)

🇨🇦 كندا: المركز الثاني (نفس الترتيب)

🇲🇽 المكسيك: المركز الثاني (هبوطًا من الأول)

🇬🇧 المملكة المتحدة: المركز الثاني (ارتفاعًا من الثالث)

🇳🇿 نيوزيلندا: المركز الثاني (ارتفاعًا من الثالث)

🇦🇺 أستراليا: المركز الثاني (ارتفاعًا من الثالث)

🇸🇦 السعودية: المركز الثاني (هبوطًا من الأول)

---

🏈 المنافسة المباشرة في توقيت البث:

واجه عرض Raw في ذلك اليوم بثًا مباشرًا لمباراة جاكسونفيل جاغوارز ضد كانساس سيتي تشيفز في دوري NFL ، والتي جذبت 22,211,000 مشاهد بإجمالي تصنيف 5.17 مقسم كالتالي:

على ABC: 12,041,000 / 1.95

على ESPN: 9,485,000 / 3.03

على ESPN2: 685,000 / 0.19

كما تزامن أيضًا مع مباراة لوس أنجلوس دودجرز ضد فيلادلفيا فيليز في دوري MLB ، التي سجلت 4,588,000 مشاهد / 0.96 (منها 3,765,000 على TBS و823,000 على TruTV).

Content:
The Bills need to get the pressure of Josh Allen. In the Bills Super Bowl years, Jim Kelly used Thurman Thomas as his relief valve, tossing screen passes to Thomas.
The current Bills should do the same. I asked ChatGPT on whether NFL teams still use the screen pass to counter blitzes.

Why screens are still used vs. the blitz

Exploit vacated space: When a defense sends extra rushers, it often leaves holes in the intermediate or flat zones. Screen passes aim to throw into those gaps, letting blockers set up downfield.

Lower risk of big negative plays: Because the pass is short and the rush is (ideally) already past the quarterback, there’s less chance of a sack or interception when executed cleanly. 

High completion percentage: Screen passes tend to be easier throws (in rhythm, with timing) and have relatively high completion rates compared to many deep passes.

Keep defenses in check: Having a credible screen threat can discourage defenses from blitzing too often, as the risk of being punished increases.
